experimentName: Torque-Speed Characteristics of a Squirrel-Cage Induction Motor

description.en: The aim of the experiment is to study the torque-speed characteristics of a three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor.

The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It also protects the circuit by automatically disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. When turned ON, it supplies electrical power to the circuit.

**Ratings:** 3P, 415 V AC, 16 A, 50 Hz

The autotransformer provides a variable AC output voltage from the 415 V input supply. During the experiment, the input voltage is increased gradually until the required voltage is reached and maintained throughout the experiment.

**Ratings:**
**Max. kVA:** 12.21, **Max. Load:** 15 A
**Input Voltage:** 415 V, 50Hz
**Output Voltage:** 0 - 450 V AC

The Tachometer displays the rotational speed of the induction motor shaft in revolutions per minute (RPM). It helps measure the motor speed at different load conditions during the experiment.

**Ratings:** 2000 RPM

The power analyzer measures the electrical parameters of the three-phase induction motor, including phase voltages, phase currents, and power. It displays the measured values for all three phases (R, Y, and B).

**Ratings:**

The motor pulley and brake drum arrangement are used to apply a mechanical load to the induction motor. The load is varied gradually using the loading mechanism, and the corresponding readings of the two spring balances (W₁ and W₂) will be observed. These readings will be used to calculate the torque developed by the motor.

**Ratings:** 415V, 2.2 kW, 4.8 A max., 1400 RPM
This table records the measured phase voltages, phase currents, power, spring balance readings (W₁ and W₂), and motor speed (RPM).

This section provides the formula used to calculate the torque developed by the three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor at different load conditions. The torque is determined from the difference between the two spring balance readings and the brake drum radius.

The Graph section displays the torque-speed characteristics of the squirrel-cage induction motor. The graph will be generated from the recorded readings and will help analyse the motor performance under different loading conditions.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical verification, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, simulation summary, the apparatus used, recorded readings, graph and the conclusion.
